title: lemur document AST
description: The contract between the lemur parser and any emitter (slides/DOM, LaTeX, HTML, …). It describes an authored *document*, not a rendered artifact: no pixels, CSS classes, DOM ids, resolved reference numbers, or step integers. Presentation is captured as neutral *intent* (roles, reveal specs, hints) that each emitter interprets. Field names are spelled out (not terse) because this is a public, human-read contract; wire size is a gzip concern, not a naming one.

astVersion.description: Contract version. An emitter refuses a version it does not understand rather than mis-rendering it.

body.description: The document as a flat sequence of blocks (Pandoc-style: sections are implied by heading levels, not nested — every emitter, LaTeX included, builds its own hierarchy from them). Slide pagination is a `pagebreak` block; it is inert for non-slide emitters.

meta.description: Neutral document metadata. What the document *is*, independent of how it is shown. An emitter decides whether to render a title page/cover from this.

presentation.description: Optional presentation *hints*. Advice a presenter/emitter MAY honour or ignore; never required to render the document. Kept separate from `meta` so the document content is not entangled with how one target displays it.

theme.description: Named theme; the emitter maps it to its own styling.

aspect.description: Aspect ratio hint, e.g. "16:9" or "4:3". No pixels: the presenter derives its design box.

across.description: Between-page transition name (opaque string the presenter maps to its own mechanism).

progress.description: Progress indicator: false/omitted = none; true = default; object = placement.

logo.description: Path/URL to a logo asset (chrome hint).

titleImage.description: Image for a synthesized title page, if the emitter makes one.

reveal.description: Progressive-disclosure intent for a block (talks reveal content step by step). Purely a *spec*; the mapping to integer steps is a per-emitter concern (a static/LaTeX emitter ignores it entirely). Grammar: comma-separated terms, each `n` (only at n), `n-` (from n), `-n` (up to n), or `n-m` (n..m). The `+`/`!pause` source sugar desugars to a spec here.

block.description: A block-level node. `reveal` (where allowed) marks progressive disclosure; `id` (where allowed) is a symbolic label for cross-references — resolution to a number/anchor is the emitter's job.

pagebreak.description: A slide-view page break (from `!slide`/`!section`). Starts a new page for a paginating emitter; ignored by flowing emitters (LaTeX/HTML article). `role` distinguishes an ordinary content page from a section-divider page.

variant.description: Neutral style variant tokens (e.g. "plain", "center"); the emitter maps them, never raw CSS classes.

heading.description: A section heading. Level implies document structure (§/§§ in LaTeX, h1–h6 in HTML); no nesting node is needed.

sublist.description: A nested list under this item (with its own ordered flag).

code.description: A code block. `source` is the raw text; splitting into lines/spans is the emitter's rendering choice. `highlights` marks line groups to emphasise progressively.

mathBlock.description: A display equation. `tex` is the raw TeX; `id` labels it for cross-reference. `marks` records named sub-spans within `tex` (an emitter may decorate them — highlight, arrow target — but the AST stays renderer-neutral).

marks.description: Named character spans inside a `tex` string, half-open `[from, to)` over the raw TeX. Nested marks are allowed (a span may contain another), and a `name` may repeat: same-named spans form a *group* an emitter realises identically (one colour, an annotation label's arrows fanning to each). The AST is neutral: how a mark is realised (a MathJax class, a LaTeX macro, or nothing) is the emitter's choice.

header.description: Render the column-heading row? '!noheader' sets false; the columns still declare separators and alignment.

figure.description: An image/figure. One source, or several stacked overlay layers (each gated by `layers[i].reveal`). `width`/`height` are author intent as a fraction/length (e.g. "44%"), not device pixels.

layers.description: Reveal spec per source beyond the first (overlay build).

anim.description: A build-time animation embedded in a slide viewport. `src` is a `lemur.anim` (wanim-style) Python module; `viewport` says where on the slide it renders — "body" (default), "full", or an "x y w h" rect. `width`/`height` are author-intent sizes (fraction/length, not pixels). The emitter runs the module to get the keyframe IR and bakes it into the viewport; each `self.next()` beat becomes a slide step (no step count in the AST).

shader.description: A live GPU shader on the slide. `src` is a GLSL fragment shader using Shadertoy's `mainImage(out vec4, in vec2)` convention (uniforms iResolution, iTime, iTimeDelta, iFrame, iMouse, plus lemur's smoothed `iStep`). `viewport` as for `anim` ("full" draws behind the slide's text). `steps` is how many slide steps it drives; `sound` an optional generative-soundtrack preset; `quality` a resolution scale. Emitters that cannot run it show a placeholder.

compute.description: A live WebGPU program on the slide. `src` is WGSL with storage buffers, `@compute` kernels (each annotated `//! threads N`, optionally `//! once`) and a `mainImage(fragCoord: vec2f) -> vec4f` that draws. `steps` is how many slide steps it drives, or "slide" to follow the slide's own step; `rate` its simulation ticks per second, `seed` its random seed, `warmup` the seconds replayed per step when jumping ahead; `viewport`, `width`, `height`, `quality` as for `shader`. Emitters that cannot run it show a placeholder.

plot.description: A figure produced by a matplotlib `!src` module, baked to a self-contained SVG at build time and placed like a figure. `width`/`height` are author-intent sizes (fraction/length, not pixels).

columns.description: Side-by-side columns. `weight` is a relative width; `style` (on the block or a column) carries symbolic style classes — e.g. the built-in `.center`/`.bottom` set a column's vertical alignment.

stack.description: Overlapping layers occupying the same space, each shown per its reveal spec (things that take each other's place).

env.description: A semantic environment (theorem, lemma, proof, example, …). `kind` names it; the emitter maps it (LaTeX `\begin{kind}`, an html box, a styled block) and decides numbering/label. `title` is an optional inline title; `body` nests any blocks, including other environments. `id` labels it for cross-reference. Neutral: an emitter with no notion of the kind can still render title + body.

styleBlock.description: A styled block (from `!style`): its `body` is any blocks, decorated by a `style`. Purely visual (no semantic label) — the emitter realises the style (html classes + inline style; LaTeX environments/`\colorbox`/macros). Built-in style classes include `.frame` (draw a box) and `.center`. `id` labels it for cross-reference.

style.description: A neutral style attribute. One rule: `.name` = a symbolic style class (built-in like `.bold`/`.center`/`.frame` or user-defined; the emitter maps each to a css class / a LaTeX macro), `color` = a foreground colour and `bg` = a background (a `#rrggbb` or css colour-name hint the emitter may honour or ignore). Names and hints only — no css, no geometry.

annotate.description: Author intent to annotate named marks (see the `mark` inline) with labels/emphasis, revealed progressively. How it is drawn (callouts + arrows, margin notes, footnotes, or nothing) is the emitter's choice — no geometry here.

mark.description: Name of the `mark` span this annotates.

color.description: Author-chosen colour hint; the emitter may ignore it.

emphasis.description: Style-class names applied to the mark as a step-gated highlight (built-in `bold`/`italic`/`underline`, or your own).

spacer.description: Vertical space (from `!gap`). `size` is a css length ('2em') or 'fill' (grow to distribute the remaining space); absent means a default single gap. Slide-view presentation intent — a manuscript emitter drops it.

connect.description: Author intent to connect named marks (see the `mark` inline) with directed, styled connectors, revealed progressively. Neutral 'link mark A to mark B' — no geometry. How it is drawn (an arrow, a plain line, or nothing) is the emitter's choice; a slide emitter draws arrows, a LaTeX/article emitter typically drops them.

dir.description: Arrowhead direction: fwd (from→to), back (to→from), both, or none (a plain line).

color.description: Author-chosen colour hint; the emitter may ignore it.

notes.description: Speaker notes: a nested body. A slide emitter may surface these in a presenter view or drop them; a manuscript emitter drops them.

bibliography.description: Bibliography entries keyed for citation. Numbering/formatting is the emitter's job.

embed.description: An escape hatch for target-specific dynamic content (a live chart, a widget). No single neutral rendering: the DOM emitter may inline `html`/`script`; a static emitter uses `fallback`. Carrying the fallback in the AST is what lets each emitter choose.

script.description: Inline JS for DOM emitters (self-contained; no network at render).

fallback.description: Static stand-in for emitters that cannot run the embed.

break.description:
A hard inline line break — '\n' in source, '
' in flowing output.

strike.description: Struck-through text (from `~~…~~`). The emitter realises it (`<s>`; LaTeX `\sout`).

underline.description: Underlined text (from `++…++`). The emitter realises it (`<u>`; LaTeX `\underline`).

xref.description: A symbolic internal cross-reference to a labelled `id` (a heading, figure, equation, or page). The parser does NOT resolve it to a number or anchor — that is the emitter's job (\ref in LaTeX, an anchor in HTML, a page link in slides). An unresolved target is an emitter-time diagnostic, not a distinct node.

content.description: Optional custom link text; otherwise the emitter supplies the resolved label/number.

cite.description: A citation of one or more bibliography keys. Symbolic; the emitter formats the marks/numbers.

prefix.description: Optional text before the citation marks (e.g. "see ").

mark.description: A named span, targetable by an `annotate`/`connect` block or by emphasis. `reveal` (optional) gates when it appears, like a block's. Neutral: an emitter with no annotation/reveal concept just renders the content.

inlineSpan.description: An unnamed inline span carrying a `style` and/or a `reveal` spec — a run of text that is coloured/emphasised or appears on a given step, without being a list item or its own block. A plain emitter just renders the content.
